p.src: Now Zhang Qing said to Wu Song, “It is not that I have a wicked heart, but rather than let you suffer in the prison camp, you would do better to let us finish off these two escorts here and stay at my house for a while. If you are willing to become an outlaw, I shall personally escort you to Precious Pearl Monastery on Two Dragon Mountain, where you can join Lu Zhishen and his band. What do you say?” Wu Song said, “Your kindness and concern for me could not be greater. But there is one thing: all my life I have sought only to fight the toughest men under heaven. These two escorts have treated me with nothing but care and attended to me throughout the journey. If I harmed them, Heaven itself would not forgive me. If you truly esteem me, then revive them both and do them no harm.” Zhang Qing replied, “Since you are so honorable and righteous, I shall revive them at once.”

p.src: Zhang Qing immediately ordered the kitchen hands to lift the two escorts from the flaying bench. Sun Erniang mixed a bowl of antidote, and Zhang Qing pulled each man by the ears and poured it down his throat. Within half an hour, the two escorts clambered to their feet as though waking from a dream. Looking at Wu Song, they said, “How did we come to be drunk here? What powerful wine they serve in this house! We drank hardly anything, yet became as drunk as this! We must remember this place and buy more from them on our return.” Wu Song burst out laughing, and Zhang Qing and Sun Erniang laughed too, while the two escorts had no idea what was going on. The two kitchen hands went off to slaughter chickens and geese, cooked them, and neatly prepared the cups, plates, and dishes.

p.src: Zhang Qing had everything set out beneath the grape arbor at the rear and arranged tables, stools, and seats. He then invited Wu Song and the two escorts into the back garden.

p.src: Wu Song gave the two escorts the seats of honor. Zhang Qing and Wu Song sat below them facing upward, while Sun Erniang sat at the side. The two men took turns pouring wine and carrying dishes back and forth. Zhang Qing urged Wu Song to drink. In the evening, he brought out the pair of Buddhist sabers and showed them to Wu Song. They were indeed forged from fine tempered iron and were no work of a single day. The two men also spoke of the exploits of heroes of the rivers and lakes—matters of killing men and setting fires. Wu Song also said, “Song Gongming of Shandong, known as the Timely Rain, upholds righteousness and freely gives away his wealth. A hero such as he has now become embroiled in trouble and fled to Squire Chai’s manor.” Hearing this, the two escorts were struck dumb with fright and could do nothing but bow to the ground. Wu Song said, “After you have taken the trouble to escort me this far, how could I possibly mean you harm? Do not be alarmed by the talk of us heroes of the rivers and lakes. We would never harm decent people. Just drink your wine. When we reach Mengzhou tomorrow, I shall see that you are rewarded.” They spent that night at Zhang Qing’s house. The next day Wu Song wished to leave, but Zhang Qing would not hear of it and kept him there, entertaining him for three days in succession. Wu Song was deeply grateful for the generous kindness of Zhang Qing and his wife. When they compared ages, Zhang Qing proved to be five years older than Wu Song, so Wu Song swore brotherhood with him and acknowledged him as elder brother. When Wu Song again took his leave, Zhang Qing prepared another feast to see him on his way; he brought out the luggage, bundle, and money pouch and returned them all; he also gave Wu Song some ten or more taels of silver, and provided the two escorts with two or three taels in small change. Wu Song then gave the entire ten taels to the two escorts as well. He put on his traveling cangue once more, and the seals were affixed as before. Zhang Qing and Sun Erniang escorted them to the door. Wu Song bade them farewell and set out for Mengzhou with the escorts. A poem says:

p.src: Before noon they had already reached the city. They went straight to the prefectural offices and submitted Dongping Prefecture’s official papers in the main hall. After reading them, the prefect took Wu Song into custody, drew up the return document himself, and sent the two escorts back; there is no need to dwell on it. He then issued orders transferring Wu Song to the local prison camp. That same day Wu Song arrived before the prison camp and saw a signboard bearing three large characters: “Anping Stockade.” The escort took Wu Song to the newcomers’ quarters, then went to submit the papers and obtain a receipt for his custody; no more need be said of it.

p.src: As soon as Wu Song entered the newcomers’ quarters, more than ten prisoners in the same condition came to see him and said, “Good fellow, you have just arrived. If your bundle contains letters of introduction or silver for expenses, take them out and keep them at hand. The warden will be here shortly, and you can give them to him. Then even if you receive the disciplinary beating, they will strike you lightly. If you have no gift for him, you will truly be in a wretched state! We are offenders just as you are, and have come especially to warn you. Have you not heard, ‘When the rabbit dies, the fox grieves; creatures mourn for their own kind’? We were only afraid that, being new, you would not understand, so we came to let you know.” Wu Song said, “Thank you all for your advice. I do have a few things with me. If he asks me civilly, I shall give him something; but if he tries to extort it from me, he will not get a single coin.” The prisoners said, “Good fellow, do not speak like that. The ancients said, ‘Fear not the magistrate, but the man who has direct charge of you.’ ‘Under another man’s low eaves, how dare you not bow your head?’ You had best be careful.” Before they had finished speaking, someone called out, “The warden is coming!” Everyone scattered.

p.src: Wu Song undid his bundle and sat in the newcomers’ quarters. Presently the man walked in and asked, “Which one is the newly arrived prisoner?” Wu Song replied, “I am.” The warden said, “You are a man with eyes and brows like anyone else, yet you insist on making me spell it out. You are the hero who killed the tiger on Jingyang Ridge and served as constable in Yanggu County. I thought you would know how the world works, but how can you be so blind to circumstance? Now that you have dared come here, not even a cat will let you strike it!” Wu Song said, “So you have come here to bluster, expecting your lord and master to give you a gift? You will not get half a coin. But I do have a fine pair of fists to give you! I have some gold and silver, but I shall keep it to buy wine for myself. Let us see what you can do to me! Surely you cannot send me back to Yanggu County for no reason!” The warden flew into a rage and left. The prisoners gathered around again and said, “Good fellow, now that you have defied him, you will suffer before long! He has gone now to report you to the commandant, and they are certain to take your life!” Wu Song said, “I am not afraid! Let him do whatever he can: if he comes at me with civil measures, I shall answer in kind; if he comes with force, I shall meet force with force!”

p.src: Before they had finished speaking, three or four men came into the solitary cell, calling for the newly arrived prisoner Wu Song. Wu Song answered, “Your lordship is right here and is not going anywhere. What are you shouting and bawling for?” The men took Wu Song along to the inspection hall, where the commandant was seated. Five or six guards brought Wu Song before him. The commandant ordered them to remove his traveling cangue and said, “You prisoner, do you know the old ordinance of Emperor Wude, our founding sovereign? Every convict newly arrived for penal service must receive one hundred warning strokes. Those assigned to hold him down, hoist him onto your backs.” Wu Song said, “None of you need make such a commotion. If you mean to beat me, then beat me; there is no need to hold me down. If I dodge so much as one stroke, I am no true man. Any strokes already dealt will not count; begin the tally again from the start. And if I utter a single cry, I am no man!” The onlookers on either side laughed. “This fool will get himself killed. Let us see how he endures it!” Wu Song added, “If you are going to beat me, strike hard. Do not give me any mercy strokes; weak blows would only leave me dissatisfied.” Everyone on both sides burst out laughing. The guard raised his cudgel and was just about to strike when a man was seen standing beside the commandant. He was over six feet tall and twenty-four or twenty-five years of age; he had a fair, clean face and three wisps of beard; a white kerchief was bound around his forehead, a gauzy blue outer robe covered his body, and one arm was supported in a sling of white silk. The man went to the commandant’s ear and quietly spoke a few words. The commandant then said, “Newly arrived prisoner Wu Song, did you fall ill with some sickness on your journey here?” Wu Song replied, “I was never ill on the road. I could drink wine, eat meat and rice, and walk perfectly well.” The commandant said, “This fellow arrived here after falling ill on the road. I see that his complexion has only just recovered, so we shall defer this round of warning strokes.” The guards who administered the cudgel whispered to Wu Song, “Quickly say that you were ill. His lordship is making an allowance for you. Just claim that you were sick and have done with it.” Wu Song said, “I was not ill, I was not ill! It would be cleaner to beat me and be done with it. I do not want this beating left on account like cudgels stored in a warehouse. Deferred, it becomes a debt gnawing at my guts—when would it ever be settled?” The onlookers on both sides all laughed. The commandant laughed as well. “Most likely this fellow suffered a fever and never managed to sweat it out; that is why he is raving. Pay him no heed. Take him away and confine him in the solitary cell for now.”

p.src: Three or four guards escorted Wu Song back to the solitary cell as before. The other prisoners all came over and asked, “Surely you have a letter from some good acquaintance to the commandant?” Wu Song said, “I have nothing of the kind.” The prisoners said, “If you have none, then deferring this beating is no kindness. Tonight they are certain to come and finish you off!” Wu Song said, “How will they come and finish me off?” The prisoners said, “At night they will bring you two bowls of dry, yellow, stale rice with some stinking dried fish. Once you have eaten your fill, they will take you to the dungeon, bind and throw you down, roll you in a dry straw mat, plug all seven of your orifices, and stand you upside down against the wall. Before half a watch has passed, your life will be ended. This is called ‘Hanging the Basin.’” Wu Song said, “What other arrangements might they make for me?” The others said, “There is another method. They bind you the same way, then fill a cloth sack with yellow sand and lay it on top of your body. Before even one watch has passed, you will be dead. This is called the ‘Earthen Sack.’” Wu Song asked again, “What other means do they have to harm me?” The others said, “Only those two are truly frightening. The rest are nothing much.”

p.src: Before they had finished speaking, a guard came in carrying a food box and asked, “Which one of you is Constable Wu, the newly transported convict?” Wu Song replied, “That is me. What do you want?” The man answered, “The commandant ordered me to bring you some refreshments.” Wu Song looked and saw a large flagon of wine, a plate of meat, a plate of noodles, and a large bowl of broth. Wu Song thought, “Could it be that they mean to let me eat these refreshments and then deal with me? Well, I may as well eat them first and see what happens afterward.” Wu Song took the flagon and drained the wine in one draught, then ate all the meat and noodles. The man gathered up the utensils and went back.

p.src: Sitting in the cell, Wu Song reflected on matters and gave a cold laugh. “Let us see how they mean to deal with me!” As evening gradually fell, the same man from before came in again with another box balanced on his head. Wu Song asked, “What have you come for this time?” The man said, “I was told to bring your evening meal.” He set out several plates of vegetables, another large flagon of wine, a large plate of fried meat, a bowl of fish soup, and a large bowl of rice. Seeing this, Wu Song thought to himself, “Once I have eaten this meal, they are certain to come and finish me off. Well, let them. Even if I die, I shall die with a full belly. I may as well eat it and reckon with them afterward.” The man waited until Wu Song had eaten, then gathered up the bowls and plates and went back.

p.src: Before long, the same man returned with another fellow. One carried a bathing tub, the other a large bucket of hot water. Looking at Wu Song, they said, “Constable, please take a bath.” Wu Song thought, “Can it be that they are waiting until I have bathed before they strike? I am not afraid of them. I may as well enjoy a wash.” The two men made the preparations and poured in the hot water. Wu Song climbed into the tub and bathed for a while. They then handed him a bathing cloth and towel, had him dry himself, and let him dress. One man emptied out the remaining water and carried the bathing tub away. The other brought in a rattan mat and gauze bed curtain and hung the curtain up; he spread the rattan mat, set down a cool pillow, bade Wu Song rest, and then went back as well.

p.src: Wu Song closed and barred the door, then pondered alone inside. “What can all this mean? Let them do as they please; I shall wait and see.” He laid down his head and went to sleep. The night passed without incident.

p.src: At daybreak, when he rose and the door was finally opened, the man from the night before came in carrying a bucket of warm water. He had Wu Song wash his face, then brought water for him to rinse his mouth. He also brought a barber with a fine-toothed comb, who combed Wu Song's hair, tied it in a topknot, and wrapped it in a headcloth. Then another man entered with a food box and took out vegetables to accompany the meal, a large bowl of meat broth, and a large bowl of rice. Wu Song thought, “Whatever game you are playing, I may as well enjoy the meal.” When Wu Song had finished eating, they served him a cup of tea. He had only just finished his tea when the man who had brought the food came and said, “This is no fit place to rest. Please move to the room over there, Constable. It will be more convenient to bring you tea and meals.” Wu Song said to himself, “So now it has come! …I will go with him for now and see what happens. …” One man came to gather up his luggage and bedding, while another led Wu Song out of the solitary cell to a place farther forward. When they pushed open the door, he saw a spotless bed and curtains within, with newly arranged tables, stools, and furnishings on either side. Wu Song entered, looked around, and thought, “I was sure they meant to throw me into an underground dungeon. How have I ended up in a place like this? It is far neater than the solitary cell!”

p.src: Wu Song sat there until noon, when the man came in again with a handled food box and a ewer of wine in his hand. Once inside the room, he opened the box and set out four kinds of fruit, a whole cooked chicken, and a quantity of steamed rolls. The man tore the cooked chicken into pieces, poured out the fine wine from the ewer, and invited the Constable to partake. Wu Song wondered, “What can this possibly mean? …” That evening they again brought him many dishes with his meal. They also invited Wu Song to bathe, then let him enjoy the cool air and rest. Wu Song thought, “The other prisoners all said the same thing, and I expected it too—so why are they treating me with such courtesy? …”

Once inside the room, he opened the box and set out four kinds of fruit, a whole cooked chicken, and a quantity of steamed rolls.
The man tore the cooked chicken into pieces, poured out the fine wine from the ewer, and invited the Constable to partake.
Wu Song wondered, “What can this possibly mean?

p.src: On the third day, food and wine were brought just as before. After breakfast that day, Wu Song went out into the stockade for a stroll. He saw that the ordinary prisoners were all carrying water, splitting firewood, or doing odd jobs, exposed beneath the clear sun. It was the blazing heat of the fifth or sixth month, with nowhere to escape it. Wu Song clasped his hands behind his back and asked, “Why are you working out here in the sun?” The prisoners all laughed and replied, “Good fellow, you do not understand. Being assigned to work here is like ascending from the mortal world to heaven! How could we dare hope to sit idle because of the heat? There are harsher men who will take you away and chain you in the main prison, where you cannot live though you beg to live, nor die though you beg to die. Even shackled with a great iron chain, you must endure it!”

p.src: After hearing them out, Wu Song walked once around the front and rear of the Hall of the Heavenly King. Beside the paper-burning furnace he saw a fine, massive block of blue stone with a socket in it, used to secure the foot of a pole. Wu Song sat on the stone for a while, then returned to his room. As he sat pondering, the man appeared again with wine and meat.

p.src: No more need be said of these details. After Wu Song moved into that room, he stayed there for several days. Every day fine wine and good food were brought for him, and there was no sign that anyone meant him harm. Wu Song could not make up his mind what it meant. At noon that day, the man brought food and wine again. Unable to bear the uncertainty any longer, Wu Song held down the box and asked him, “Whose household attendant are you? Why do you keep bringing food and wine to entertain me?” The man replied, “I reported this to you the other day, Constable. I am a trusted servant in the commandant's household.” Wu Song said, “Then let me ask you this: who exactly tells you to bring me food and wine every day? And what is meant to happen after I have eaten it?” The man said, “It is the young commandant of the commandant's household who ordered it sent for you, Constable.” Wu Song said, “I am a convicted prisoner and have never done the commandant the slightest service. Why should he send me things to eat?” The man said, “How would a humble servant like me know? The young commandant instructed me to keep bringing it for three months or half a year, and only then speak of the matter.” Wu Song said, “That is stranger still! Surely they do not mean to feed me until I am fat and then finish me off. What a damned riddle! How am I supposed to solve it? When I do not know the reason for this food and wine, how can I consume it with an easy mind? Just tell me this: what sort of man is your young commandant? Where has he ever met me? Once you tell me, I will eat his food and drink his wine.” The man said, “When you first arrived the other day, Constable, there was a man standing in the hall with a white kerchief around his head and his right hand bound up. That was the young commandant.” Wu Song said, “Do you mean the man in the blue gauze outer robe who stood beside the commandant?” The man replied, “Precisely. He is the elder commandant's son.” Wu Song said, “When I was about to receive the initiation beating, was it he who spoke up and saved me?” The man said, “It was. The young commandant spoke to his father, and that is why you were not beaten, Constable.” Wu Song said, “That is curious indeed! I am from Qinghe County, while he is from Mengzhou. We have never known each other. There must be some reason why he treats me with such favor. Let me ask you: what is the young commandant's surname and given name?” The man said, “His surname is Shi and his given name is En. He is highly skilled with fist and staff, and everyone calls him Shi En, the ‘Golden-Eyed Tiger Cub.’” On hearing this, Wu Song said, “He must be a fine man. Go and ask him to come out and meet me; then I will accept this food and wine from you. If you do not bring him out to meet me, I will not touch a single morsel.” The man said, “The young commandant instructed me not to reveal the details. I was to wait three months or half a year before telling you and arranging a meeting.” Wu Song said, “Nonsense! Just go and ask the young commandant to come out. Once he has met me, that will settle the matter.” The man was afraid and refused to go. Wu Song lost his temper, and the man had no choice but to go inside and report the matter.

p.src: After some time, Shi En came running out from within and bowed as soon as he saw Wu Song. Wu Song hurriedly returned the courtesy and said, “I am merely a prisoner under your father’s authority and have never before had the honor of making your acquaintance. The other day I was spared a severe beating through your kindness, and now you provide me with fine food and wine every day. I am wholly undeserving of it. Nor have you given me the least task to perform. I am truly receiving reward without merit, and can neither sleep nor eat in peace.” Shi En replied, “I have long heard your illustrious name, elder brother—it has rung in my ears like thunder. I only regretted that the great distance between us kept me from meeting you. Today I am fortunate enough to have you here and have wished to pay my respects in person. But I was ashamed that I had nothing worthy with which to entertain you, and so dared not come to see you.” Wu Song asked, “Just now I heard your attendant say that Wu Song should be allowed to rest for three or six months, and then something would be discussed. What is it that the young commandant wishes to tell me?” Shi En said, “That rustic servant has no discretion and blurted it out to you. How could I speak of the matter so rashly?” Wu Song said, “If you carry on like this, Commandant, you are merely playing the coy scholar! You will make Wu Song’s belly burst from pent-up vexation. How am I to endure it? Just tell me plainly what you want me to do.” Shi En said, “Since the servant has let it slip, I must tell you. Because you are a great and true man, elder brother, there is a certain matter in which I wish to ask your help—no one but you could accomplish it. But you have come a long way and your strength is diminished, not yet fully restored. Please recuperate for three or five months, perhaps half a year. Once your strength is fully restored, I shall tell you the whole matter in detail.” Hearing this, Wu Song laughed heartily. “Hear me, Commandant! Last year, after suffering malaria for three months, I killed a great tiger on Jingyang Ridge while drunk, and needed no more than three punches and a couple of kicks to beat it dead. How much less need you worry today!” Shi En said, “I still cannot tell you now. Rest and recover a while longer, elder brother. When your honored body is completely sound, only then shall I dare tell you.” Wu Song said, “So you still think I have no strength. If that is what you say, then tell me: the stone block I saw yesterday before the Hall of the Heavenly King—about how much does it weigh?” Shi En said, “I should think it weighs four or five hundred catties.” Wu Song said, “Come with me and let us have a look. Wu Song would like to see whether he can lift it.” Shi En said, “Please finish your wine first, and then we shall go together.” Wu Song said, “Let us go now. It will not be too late to drink when we return.”

p.src: The two came before the Hall of the Heavenly King. When the prisoners saw Wu Song arriving with the young commandant, they all bowed and offered greetings. Wu Song gave the stone block a slight shake, then laughed and said, “I truly have grown soft and feeble. How could I possibly lift it?” Shi En said, “How could a stone weighing three to five hundred catties be taken lightly?” Wu Song laughed. “Young Commandant, do you truly believe I cannot lift it? All of you stand back and watch Wu Song try.” Wu Song stripped off his upper garments and tied them around his waist. Then, with a single embrace of the stone block, he lifted it easily from the ground. With both hands he hurled it down, driving it more than a foot into the earth with a thud. At the sight, all the prisoners were astounded. Wu Song reached down with his right hand and pulled the block from the earth, then tossed it into the air until it rose more than ten feet above the ground. He caught it in both hands and gently set it back in its original place. He turned to face Shi En and the prisoners. His face was not flushed, his heart was not pounding, and his breath was perfectly calm. Shi En stepped forward, embraced Wu Song, and bowed to him, saying, “Elder brother, you are no ordinary mortal! You are truly a god from heaven!” All the prisoners bowed together and cried, “Truly, a divine man!” A poem says:

p.src: Shi En then invited Wu Song into the main hall of his private residence and asked him to be seated. Wu Song said, “This time, Young Commandant, you must tell me: what business do you wish me to undertake?” Shi En said, “Please sit a little while. When my honored father comes out to meet you, I may then trouble you with the full account.” Wu Song said, “If you want a man to do something, do not behave with such maidenly hesitation. Acting so contrary to sense, you are no man for getting things done. Even if the business means knives and bloodshed, Wu Song will do it for you! But if there is any fawning deceit in it, I am no man!” Shi En remained standing with hands respectfully clasped before his breast, and only then told him the whole affair. And so Wu Song was destined to display once more his deadly skill and again unleash the awesome might with which he had slain the tiger. Indeed: where his twin fists rise, clouds and thunder roar; when his flying feet strike, wind and rain recoil. What matter did Shi En finally reveal to Wu Song? Listen to the next chapter for the explanation.
